newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Hijacker seizes Russian bus in Caucasus.
newsitem.headline: Hijacker seizes Russian bus in Caucasus.

text.p: An armed man seized 30 hostages aboard a bus in the southern Russian region of Dagestan, neighbouring Chechnya, on Monday, the Russian Emergencies Ministry said.

A spokesman told Reuters that the unidentified man, who was carrying an assault rifle and a hand grenade, had demanded a helicopter. The bus was hijacked near the airport serving the Dagestani capital of Makhachkala on the Caspian Sea.
The ministry spokesman could give no other details of the incident.
Such hijackings have not been uncommon in Russia's turbulent North Caucasus. Many but by no means all have involved Chechens fighting for independence for their mainly Moslem region.
Last September a man armed with a grenade hijacked a bus in Makhachkala and demanded a helicopter. He fled by car to Chechnya after freeing them and taking a local politician along as security.

There were two major and bloody hostage-takings on Russian soil during the 1994-1996 Chechen war, one of them in Dagestan. Before the war broke out, there were a series of bus hijackings for ransom conducted by Chechen bandits across the North Caucausus.
